question.worked_solution:
First, note that the denominator's conjugate is $1+\sqrt{1-t}.$

Now, to rationalize the denominator, we multiply both the numerator and denominator by the conjugate $1+\sqrt{1-t},$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3t}{1-\sqrt{1-t}} & = \\ \frac{3t}{1-\sqrt{1-t}}\cdot \frac{1+\sqrt{1-t}}{1+\sqrt{1-t}} & = \\ \frac{3t(1+\sqrt{1-t})}{(1-\sqrt{1-t})(1+\sqrt{1-t})} & = \\ \frac{3t(1+\sqrt{1-t})}{{1}^{2}-(\sqrt{1-t})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{3t(1+\sqrt{1-t})}{1-(1-t)} & = \\ \frac{3\cancel{t}(1+\sqrt{1-t})}{\cancel{t}} & = \\ 3(1+\sqrt{1-t}) & \end{aligned}
$$
